w: Guns once covered the mouth of Marsamxett Harbour from this polygonal fort, raised by the Knights of St John in 1793-95 -- one of the oldest of its kind anywhere. The British reworked it through the 19th century, the army held it until 1979, and it now sits on Malta's UNESCO tentative list.
s: Knights' fort guarding Marsamxett Harbour since 1795

w: Raised in 1552 to guard Senglea's landward approach, this small fort took the weight of the Great Siege of Malta in 1565 before being rebuilt as a cavalier, completed in 1581. The 20th century tore most of it down -- only the base survives, a fragment of one of the island's defining battles.
s: Fort that survived the 1565 Great Siege of Malta

w: A steel arch strides from Fort St Elmo's foreshore out to the breakwater guarding Grand Harbour's mouth -- built in 2011-12 to replace the 1906 span that stood here until German bombs took it out in 1941. Same crossing, same view down the harbour entrance, rebuilt seven decades on.
s: Grand Harbour footbridge rebuilt after WWII took the original
_facts: single-span arched truss steel footbridge from Fort Saint Elmo's foreshore to the breakwater at the Grand Harbour entrance

w: Once known as Bishop's Island, this speck in Marsamxett Harbour took its current name from the fort the Portuguese Grand Master António Manoel de Vilhena raised here in the 1720s -- the fortress's name outlasting whatever the bishop did to earn the first one.
s: Harbour island renamed after its 1720s fort
